title: School Notebooks 5-pack

drivers.name: Store closed Monday
drivers.evidence: Store closure on Monday reduces available sales days; no direct past closure data, so apply conservative estimate based on 1/7 day loss. Historical price increases show no lift; no promotion. Noise-adjusted effect shrunk to x0.85 (15% downside).

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 7.8. The target week has no events, but the store is closed Monday, likely reducing sales. The price is up 2.3%, which historically has not driven lift (past price increase in 2026-09-28: 10 units, vs baseline 7.8 → x1.28, but no promotion). The Halloween effect from the prior week is noise-adjusted x0.98 (1 past occurrence), but it's not a direct driver here. No promotion. The closed day suggests a downward bias. The classical model’s x0.98 is reasonable but doesn’t account for the closed day. We adjust down for the closure (1 day out of 7), using past closure impact evidence: none, so shrink toward 1.0. Final adjustment: slight downside. Noise-adjusted effect is uncertain.

brief:
PRODUCT: School Notebooks 5-pack | category Office | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25 (2 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 9.03 (+2.3% vs regular price 8.83)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 7.8 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 27.2 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 18.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-64% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
